title: Rolling-horizon staffing allocator and scope compact playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: Provide a pragmatic, repeatable playbook and lightweight tooling for allocating staff across overlapping product cycles using a rolling-horizon model. The goal is to reduce ad-hoc scope cuts, make trade-offs transparent, and provide a bounded surge capacity while keeping the organization aligned to OKRs.

Scope: This ticket delivers the playbook, templates, and a small Google Sheet prototype (staffing allocator) that PMs and ENG leads can use to: 1) define a 6-week rolling horizon, 2) nominate critical-path work, 3) assign fractional staffing slices, 4) designate a surge cordon (bench pool) with release triggers, and 5) produce a scope-compact recommendation when headcount is constrained.

Key components delivered:
- Playbook doc describing roles (Lead PM, Cycle Owner, Surge Steward, Eng Patch), decision gates, and communication cadence.
- Staffing allocator spreadsheet prototype (Drive link included) with inputs: role FTEs, skill tags, blocking dependencies, and derived outputs: allocation ledger, projected capacity delta, and suggested scope scraps.
- A triage matrix template for scope cuts that ranks work by customer impact, OKR alignment, downstream dependencies, and unblock complexity.
- A one-page reporting card for weekly syncs: committed vs. planned points, scope drift, and surge consumption.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Playbook reviewed and approved by PM leadership and two engineering managers.
2) Spreadsheet prototype tested in two cross-functional cycle planning sessions and applied to at least one real tranche.
3) Two example scope-compaction decisions recorded with rationale and communicated to stakeholders.
4) A minimal RFC submitted to docs/confluence with links to artifacts and a short walkthrough video.

Approach and mechanics:
- Rolling horizon window: default 6 weeks (configurable). Weeks are chunked into tranches: immediate (0-2), near (3-4), horizon (5-6).
- Capacity slices: allocate people in fractional slices (e.g., 0.2 FTE) per tranche; freeze allocations 10 days prior to tranche start unless explicit freeze exception raised.
- Surge cordon: maintain a 8-12% bench of engineering hours as surge; surge consumption is gated by an approval flow documented in the playbook.
- Scope compaction: when capacity delta < -1 FTE across critical-path items, run triage matrix and propose either (a) defer, (b) de-scope to minimal MVI, or (c) reassign to surge. All proposals must include customer impact and OKR delta.

Decision points and trade-offs:
- Default to engineer-validated estimates; where estimates differ >30% across leads, flag for re-estimation rather than blind cuts.
- Tighter freeze windows increase predictability but reduce flexibility for urgent issues; recommended default freeze at -10 days with emergency review route.

Metrics / Signals to track post-rollout:
- Cycle on-time hit-rate (percent of committed deliverables shipped on tranche date).
- Scope slippage (story points deferred vs planned).
- Surge burn rate and average time-to-approve surge use.
- Number of ad-hoc reassignments per cycle (target < 2).

Artifacts / links: 
- Confluence draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/Rolling+Horizon+Playbook (draft)
- Allocator spreadsheet (prototype): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/drive-proto/rolling-horizon-allocator (sheet v0.2)
- Example scope compaction notes (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/example-compactions
- Initial RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/312

Follow-ups after acceptance:
- Integrate the allocator into the cycle planning template in Confluence; add a short how-to video.
- Collect feedback from three cycles and iterate playbook (v1 -> v2).
- Explore a lightweight Redwood Console integration for cycle-level capacity snapshots (scoping only).
